name: Optimised FSAE-style rear corner (rear-left)
description: Phase 9: upper ball joint lowered 6 mm so a real spherical bearing housing (13 mm radius) fits inside the 10 inch rim with 2 mm to spare (camber gain -0.43 -> -0.38 deg/10 mm, roll centre about 7 mm lower); static camber then set to -1.75 deg to keep the outside tyre at about -1 deg at 1.5 g, and the inner tie rod (toe link) end nudged about 1 mm to cancel the extra bump steer. Phase 7: output of `suspkin optimize data/baseline_fsae_rear.json data/optimize_rear.json` (anti-squat -0.4% -> 25%, anti-lift under braking -0.1% -> 9%, RC migration -0.38 -> -0.03, toe change over +/-50 mm 0.13 -> 0.01 deg), then hand-finished: pushrod outer end moved up to stay 14.5 mm above the raised lower arm, a 4.0 N m/deg rear anti-roll bar (same layout as the front) for ~52% front lateral load transfer, static camber -1.65 deg so the outside tyre is at about -1 deg at 1.5 g, and the upper ball joint lowered 1.5 mm to keep it inside the rim at that camber.
coordinate_system: SAE/ISO vehicle axes: +X forward, +Y left, +Z up. Origin on the ground plane, on the car centerline, at the REAR axle line.

packaging._note: 10 inch rim envelope, checked in the wheel's own frame (see solver/suspkin/packaging.py)

vehicle._note: Whole-car numbers (see solver/suspkin/sideview.py). Same made-up car as the front file; this corner is on the driven rear axle with a chassis-mounted diff and outboard brakes. spring_rate_n_per_mm is one rear corner's spring (40 N/mm, about 230 lb/in). Car-level numbers (mass, weight split, design g) are read from the FRONT file by `suspkin car`.

point_descriptions.RTI: Toe link inner end (fixed on the chassis)
point_descriptions.RTO: Toe link outer end (on the upright, behind the axle)
point_descriptions.PRO: Pushrod outer end (bracket on the lower A-arm)
point_descriptions.RKP: Rocker pivot (on its rotation axis, on the chassis)

rocker._note: Pushrod and rocker (bellcrank). The rocker spins about 'axis' through RKP. See solver/suspkin/rocker.py.

arb._note: Rear anti-roll bar (U-bar), same layout as the front: a drop link from ARL on the rocker to the end of the bar's arm (ARA); the arm joins the bar at ARP and the bar runs across the car (Y axis). See solver/suspkin/arb.py. Rate chosen in Phase 7 with `suspkin car` for ~52% front lateral load transfer.
